title: Duplicate customer emails from the notification service
context: A notification-service consumes send jobs from a message queue and calls an external email provider's batch-send API. Each job is one provider call with up to 2,000 recipients. Worker pools run in eu-west (pool-a and pool-b) and us-east. On Sep 19 customers began reporting duplicate emails. The team must work out which conditions produce duplicates and what to change.

entities.description: Message queue holding send jobs; supports a per-queue-consumer visibility timeout.
Renders marketing email bodies before a send job is queued.

evidence.text: About 38,000 duplicate email sends were identified for Sep 18-19. All duplicated sends were processed by eu-west workers.

Sep 17 10:00: the queue visibility timeout for eu-west pool-a was lowered from 300 s to 60 s to speed up recovery from crashed workers. The plan was to apply the same change to eu-west pool-b next and then to us-east.
From Sep 18 06:00 the provider validates recipients synchronously for requests with more than 500 recipients. Requests with 500 or fewer recipients are unaffected.

evidence.source: duplicate analysis by message type (eu-west, Sep 18-19)
evidence.text: Duplicate rate: marketing sends 3.2%; transactional sends 0.00%.
Duplicate rate: eu-west 2.1%; us-east 0.01% (the long-run baseline is 0.01%).

p99 provider call duration for requests with more than 500 recipients: 26 s before Sep 18 06:00 and 95 s after. For requests with 500 or fewer recipients: 12 s both before and after. Durations are the same in all three pools.

The Sep 17 change never reached eu-west pool-b: its configuration push failed without alerting, and pool-b is still at 300 s. us-east is at 300 s. Pool-b processes about 40% of eu-west jobs with the same mix of message types and batch sizes as pool-a.
Duplicate rate for jobs with more than 500 recipients: 4.4%. For jobs with 500 or fewer recipients: 0.01%.

evidence.source: duplicate analysis, eu-west pool-b and us-east (Sep 18-19)
evidence.text: Duplicate rate for jobs with more than 500 recipients: pool-b 0.01%, us-east 0.01%. For jobs with 500 or fewer recipients: pool-b 0.00%, us-east 0.01%.
On Sep 17, after pool-a moved to 60 s and before the provider change, the duplicate rate was 0.01% in every pool, including for pool-a jobs with more than 500 recipients.
Transactional jobs always have 50 or fewer recipients. Marketing jobs range from 50 to 2,000 recipients; about 60% of marketing jobs have more than 500.

A worker deletes a job from the queue only after the provider call returns. If a job is not deleted within the visibility timeout it becomes visible again and can be received by another worker. The provider does not de-duplicate repeated requests.
Pool-a has 24 workers, pool-b 16, and us-east 30. No analysis relates the number of idle workers to how quickly a re-visible job is picked up or to the duplicate rate.
"The provider slowdown hit every region. This is the provider's bug and it is what is causing the duplicates."
"Pool-a ran on 60 s for all of Sep 17 with zero extra duplicates. The timeout change is proven safe."
eu-west network maintenance on Sep 18 from 02:00 to 03:00 caused brief packet loss between worker hosts and the queue.
Template engine v2 went live for all marketing emails in all regions on Sep 16.
Personal data of EU customers must be processed only by eu-west infrastructure.
The provider allows 50 calls per second per account; current peak usage is 4 calls per second.

hypotheses.text: A 60 s visibility timeout is sufficient on its own to produce elevated duplicate sends.
The provider's slower handling of requests above 500 recipients is sufficient on its own to produce elevated duplicate sends.
A 60 s visibility timeout together with provider call durations above 60 s is sufficient to produce elevated duplicate sends.
Marketing content or templates raise the duplicate rate independently of recipient count.
Among jobs whose provider call outlasts the visibility timeout, pool worker count affects the duplicate rate.
A 120 s visibility timeout would prevent all elevated duplicates for jobs above 500 recipients under current provider behaviour.

edges.to: call duration for jobs with 500 or fewer recipients

actions.text: Return eu-west pool-a's visibility timeout to 300 s.
Split marketing jobs so that no provider call has more than 500 recipients.
Route eu-west marketing jobs to the us-east pool until the incident is resolved.
Pause all marketing sends in every region until provider latency returns to normal.
Complete the planned rollout of the 60 s visibility timeout to eu-west pool-b and us-east.
Roll marketing emails back to template engine v1.
